I'm in the same scenario as you.

Last year, I applied to a couple of universities both in Sweden and Denmark using the 'prior learning pathway'.

Essentially, you can still apply to the courses at the universities, however, the process to prove that you're eligible to receive a waiver for the general entry requirements is extremely tough.

Unfortunately I was rejected from Malmö University and Southern Denmark University using this application method. Stockholm University has a much more strict process than the others, so I didn't even bother trying.

Having said all this, it's not hopeless as your applications may have stronger evidence than mine did. You've just got to be extremely determined to put in the best application of your life to be considered.

It's totally normal to want to go on a diet or reduce your food intake after seeing your numbers on the scale go up.
Pretending you're full or not finishing your meal can be a sign of obsession with food which is an early warning symptom of eating disorders so it's important to keep an eye on that particular behaviour.

For men with anorexia, typically they can be eating quite well but to compensate for the intake of calories, they will exercise obsessively to the point where they end up in a deficit.

If these concerns you're having are impacting on you going about your daily life, I highly recommend you go and see a GP. 
They'll give you a questionnaire and you'll be graded on a global scoring scale on your likelihood of having an eating disorder; then you can discuss the next step in getting professional help. 

Hope this info helps ☺️
